text:
Maria: Heads up — opened a tiny docs PR to consolidate 429 fallback examples into one migration guide. WIP link: http://go/doc/429-migrate

Akshay: Nice. Can we include the SDK snippets for python/node? Current examples are scattered and out of sync.

Maria: Yes. I'll add both. Pasting a quick python sketch (will update after feedback):
```python
# python snippet: simplified retry example
try:
    resp = client.generate(model='gpt-large', input=prompt)
except ApiError as e:
    if getattr(e, 'code', None) == 429:
        # fallback: shorten prompt or route to smaller model
        resp = client.generate(model='gpt-small', input=short_prompt)
```

Ben: Small nit — avoid implying the SDK returns `status_code` on success. New SDK surfaces errors as exceptions (ApiError). Use `getattr(e, 'code', None) == 429` like you show. Also add a note about not swallowing other transient errors.

Maria: Good catch. I'll tweak wording. Also going to add a short migration note about context-window trims and prompt-eviction behavior when clients hit hard context limits.

June: Can we also flag the stale cross-links? The old runbook has several orphan links to the beta 'rate-limits' pages. We should canonicalize to /docs/reference/rate-limits and /docs/ops/streaming-resume.

Akshay: @Maria could you include an example router policy for canary fallback? e.g., route to `gpt-small` when dedicated pool is saturated. Helps platform teams replicate.

Maria: Yep — drafting a tiny YAML snippet for the router policy: 
```yaml
route:
  priority: latency
  fallbacks:
    - model: gpt-small
      max_latency_ms: 300
```

docs-bot: Reminder: PR size threshold for docs website is 1000 lines. If the snippet set causes a big diff, split SDK examples into `_includes/snippets/429/*`.

Maria: Thanks, docs-bot — I'll split if needed and move heavy examples to includes.

Ben: Support asked to document how to map 429 -> 503 in proxy layers so frontend doesn't bubble noisy 429s directly to users. Can you add a short recommended proxy rule?

June: Also add a small diagnostics checklist for triage: minimal repro, sequence length, token counts, rate histogram, which model ID and region. That'll speed QA and support investigations.

Akshay: I'll add unit harnesses for node/python snippets into the examples repo so snippets are runnable.

Maria: Quick question — does anyone have a public-safe link for 'prefix caching' behavior? The internal KB is private. For public docs I can add a short explainer and link to the cache behavior section instead of the private note.

June: Use `http://intra/redwood/kv-cache-tricks` internally. For public copy we should write a brief paragraph explaining prefix/KV caching and point to the 'caching' appendix.

Ben: :thumbsup: When the PR is up I'll do a focused review on the error-mapping language and SDK examples.

Maria: Pushed PR: https://git/repo/docs/pulls/456 — added checklist to PR description and split snippets into `_includes/snippets/429/`. Ping me with inline comments.

deploy-bot: deploy-preview created — https://deploys/redwood-docs/preview/456

Akshay: Found one stray link in the 'error mapping' table pointing to the old beta page. I'll open a follow-up tiny PR to replace that anchor.

Maria: OK, plan: merge after Ben's sanity review and we can follow with the small link-fix PR. Thanks everyone :rocket:

Ben: Quick follow-up review incoming. If anything's ambiguous I'll request a wording tweak rather than block.

June: Adding the triage checklist to the runbook as a short collapsible section.

Maria: Great — closing out here. Will add a short changelog entry under 'Docs' for the migration guide and the snippet locations.
